```{r}
#| label: setup
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

# Read the small prepared file once when the app starts.
# prepare_data.R shows how it was selected from the official source.
df <- read_csv("fuel_economy.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
addResourcePath("www", normalizePath("www"))

# Reuse the same empty-selection message in every plot.
empty_plot <- function(message = "No vehicles match these filters.") {
  plotly_empty() %>%
    layout(title = list(text = message, y = .5),
           xaxis = list(visible = FALSE), yaxis = list(visible = FALSE))
}
```

# {.sidebar width="280px"}

Compare EPA vehicle configurations from **2015–2025**.
All five controls filter every plot, value box, and data row.

```{r}
#| label: five-input-types
# 1. Dropdown: focus on one manufacturer or keep all manufacturers.
selectInput("make", "Manufacturer", choices = c("All", sort(unique(df$make))))

# 2. Checkboxes: choose one or several broad vehicle groups.
checkboxGroupInput("groups", "Vehicle groups",
                   choices = c("Cars", "SUVs", "Pickups", "Vans", "Other"),
                   selected = c("Cars", "SUVs", "Pickups", "Vans", "Other"),
                   inline = TRUE)

# 3. Slider: choose the model-year range.
sliderInput("years", "Model years", min = 2015, max = 2025,
            value = c(2015, 2025), step = 1, sep = "")

# 4. Radio buttons: choose a fuel group.
radioButtons("fuel", "Fuel", choices = c("Both", "Gasoline", "Diesel"),
             selected = "Both", inline = TRUE)

# 5. Numeric input: set the maximum engine displacement.
numericInput("engine_max", "Maximum engine size (liters)",
             value = max(df$engine_l), min = .5,
             max = max(df$engine_l), step = .1)

textOutput("selection_note")
```

# About the Data {scrolling=true}

## Source and scope

::: {.card title="FuelEconomy.gov data"}

![FuelEconomy.gov - the official government source for fuel economy information](www/fuel_economy_source.png){width=320}

**Source and image:** [FuelEconomy.gov](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/download.shtml),
administered by Oak Ridge National Laboratory for DOE and EPA.
[Variable definitions](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/ws/).
Data downloaded November 18, 2026. This is a student project using their data.

The prepared file contains **12,381 vehicle configurations** from model years
2015–2025. Each row is an EPA vehicle configuration, identified by its record
ID. Rows are not vehicles sold or individual drivers. Different engines,
transmissions, and drive systems can give the same model multiple rows.

The project includes single-fuel gasoline and diesel configurations with
positive city MPG, highway MPG, combined MPG, and engine displacement.
Gasoline includes regular, premium, and midgrade fuel. Non-plug-in hybrids
are included. Electric, plug-in hybrid, flexible-fuel, and other dual-fuel
configurations are excluded. The preparation script is `prepare_data.R`.

:::

## How to read the results

::: {.card title="Definitions and limitations"}

**MPG** means miles per U.S. gallon. Higher MPG means the vehicle travels
farther on a gallon of fuel. Combined MPG uses the source's `comb08` value;
it is not calculated as the simple average of city and highway MPG.

The broad groups are Cars (including station wagons and two-seaters), SUVs,
Pickups, Vans (including minivans), and Other. The original EPA class stays
in the searchable table.

Every mean gives each configuration equal weight. These are **not
sales-weighted averages**. Differences by manufacturer, engine size, fuel,
or year can reflect a different mix of configurations and hybrid technology.
The comparisons describe this dataset and do not show causal effects.

Plot 3 ranks at most ten manufacturers that have at least five selected
configurations. Hover over a bar to see its count. If fewer than five
configurations remain for every manufacturer, it explains why no ranking
is shown. The table's own search further narrows the table display only;
use the sidebar to filter the entire dashboard.

:::

```{r}
#| label: server
#| context: server

# One reactive dataset keeps all dashboard outputs on the same selection.
filtered <- reactive({
  req(input$make, input$years, input$fuel, input$engine_max)
  d <- df %>%
    filter(vehicle_group %in% input$groups,
           year >= input$years[1], year <= input$years[2],
           engine_l <= input$engine_max)
  if (input$make != "All") d <- d %>% filter(make == input$make)
  if (input$fuel != "Both") d <- d %>% filter(fuel == input$fuel)
  d
})

# Three value boxes use exactly the same rows as the plots.
output$selection_note <- renderText({
  paste(format(nrow(filtered()), big.mark = ","), "configurations selected")
})
output$n_value <- renderText(format(nrow(filtered()), big.mark = ","))
output$mpg_value <- renderText({
  if (nrow(filtered()) == 0) "-" else sprintf("%.1f", mean(filtered()$combined_mpg))
})
output$gap_value <- renderText({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) "-" else sprintf("%.1f", mean(d$highway_mpg - d$city_mpg))
})

# The findings paragraph updates instead of keeping stale numbers after a filter.
output$findings <- renderUI({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(tags$p("No configurations match these filters. Select a vehicle group or widen the filters."))
  class_summary <- d %>% group_by(vehicle_group) %>%
    summarise(median_mpg = median(combined_mpg), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(median_mpg), vehicle_group)
  highest <- class_summary[1, ]
  tags$p(sprintf(
    "These %s configurations average %.1f combined MPG. The mean highway-minus-city difference is %.1f MPG. Among the selected vehicle groups, %s has the highest median combined MPG at %.1f. These results compare configurations equally; they are not sales-weighted averages, and vehicle mix can affect the comparisons.",
    format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), mean(d$combined_mpg),
    mean(d$highway_mpg - d$city_mpg), highest$vehicle_group, highest$median_mpg))
})

# Plot 1: Summarise each model year, then draw its mean combined MPG.
output$trend <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  yearly <- d %>% group_by(year, fuel) %>%
    summarise(mean_mpg = mean(combined_mpg), configurations = n(), .groups = "drop")
  p <- ggplot(yearly, aes(year, mean_mpg, color = fuel, group = fuel,
                          text = paste("Year:", year, "<br>Fuel:", fuel,
                                       "<br>Configurations:", configurations,
                                       "<br>Mean combined MPG:", round(mean_mpg, 1)))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2025, 2)) +
    labs(x = "Model year", y = "Mean combined MPG", color = "Fuel")
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
})

# Plot 2: Compare the median and spread, rather than only group averages.
output$by_class <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(reorder(vehicle_group, combined_mpg, FUN = median), combined_mpg)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "#3D7EA6", outlier.alpha = .3) + coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "Vehicle group", y = "Combined MPG")
  ggplotly(p)
})

# Plot 3: Compare manufacturer means, keeping groups with at least five rows.
output$by_make <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  manufacturers <- d %>% group_by(make) %>%
    summarise(mean_mpg = mean(combined_mpg), configurations = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(configurations >= 5) %>% arrange(desc(mean_mpg), make) %>% slice_head(n = 10)
  if (nrow(manufacturers) == 0) return(empty_plot("Ranking needs at least 5 configurations per manufacturer."))
  p <- ggplot(manufacturers, aes(reorder(make, mean_mpg), mean_mpg,
           text = paste(make, "<br>Mean combined MPG:", round(mean_mpg, 1),
                        "<br>Configurations:", configurations))) +
    geom_col(fill = "#3D7EA6") + coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "Manufacturer (at least 5 selected configurations)", y = "Mean combined MPG")
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
})

# Plot 4: Check the association between engine displacement and MPG.
output$engine <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(engine_l, combined_mpg, color = fuel,
                     text = paste(year, make, model, "<br>Engine:", engine_l,
                                  "L<br>Combined MPG:", combined_mpg,
                                  "<br>Technology:", technology))) +
    geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1.2) +
    labs(x = "Engine size (liters)", y = "Combined MPG", color = "Fuel")
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
})

# Plot 5: Above the dashed line means higher highway MPG than city MPG.
output$driving <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(city_mpg, highway_mpg, color = fuel,
                     text = paste(year, make, model, "<br>City MPG:", city_mpg,
                                  "<br>Highway MPG:", highway_mpg))) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray45") +
    geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1.2) +
    labs(x = "City MPG", y = "Highway MPG", color = "Fuel")
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
})

# The table shares the sidebar filters and also has its own search box.
output$vehicles_table <- renderDT({
  filtered() %>% select(year, make, model, vehicle_group, fuel, technology,
                        engine_l, city_mpg, highway_mpg, combined_mpg,
                        epa_class, transmission, drive, id) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE,
      colnames = c("Year", "Manufacturer", "Model", "Group", "Fuel", "Technology",
                   "Engine (L)", "City MPG", "Highway MPG", "Combined MPG",
                   "EPA class", "Transmission", "Drive", "Record ID"),
      options = list(pageLength = 10, searching = TRUE, paging = TRUE,
                     dom = "lftip", scrollX = TRUE,
                     language = list(info = "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ configurations",
                       infoFiltered = "(filtered from _MAX_ selected configurations)")))
}, server = TRUE)
```
